_README: THE REPORT CONTRACT — one shape for every bug / feature / capability report
in the suite. This file is MIRRORED BYTE-IDENTICALLY into every repo that
owns a report queue (LeapHQ, pikpak-fleet-dashboard, leap-daily-report,
stoppageviewer, PlacementImageViewer). Each side has a test that reads it
and asserts its own serialiser emits this shape and its own UI consumes it.
Same idea as tests/fixtures/report_payload.json in the fleet<->daily-report
split and security-headers.json in this repo: the fixture IS the contract,
so a change to it is a reviewable line in a diff rather than a surprise in
Changing this file means changing it in every repo. If a field must differ
per app, it does not belong here.
_version: v2, 2026-09-16 — settled BEFORE the fixture was mirrored into the other
four repos, because every one of these is a one-repo edit today and a
five-repo edit afterwards. v1 lived for one day and one repo.
is what the server enforces EXACTLY (with `offered` split out as what the

_statuses: The lifecycle every store shares. LeapHQ ran open|triaged|resolved until
2026-09-16 and could not decline a report at all, while every plug-in
could — so a declined plug-in row was unreachable in core's filter and
federation had to stay read-only. Four statuses, one vocabulary.
_closedStatuses: What 'still waiting on a human' means, by exclusion. A status NOT listed
here is treated as open — including one this contract has never heard of,
because a triage list that silently drops an unrecognised report is the
_transitions: What the SERVER must accept, exactly — not a floor. v1 of this contract
said 'a server may accept more', which let two apps behave differently
while both conforming: LeapHQ refuses open -> resolved, and every
bug-report-py server accepts any of the four because it validates the
status and not the move. A contract that permits that is not settling
anything. If a transition belongs, put it in this map.
_offered: What the triage UI must SHOW from each status — a subset of the map
above, because not every legal move is worth a button. `triaged -> open`
is the escape hatch: legal, but a Reopen button on a triaged row reads
as a mistake, so it is reachable through the API and not offered.
Declining captures a reason, carried as the audit row's `note`.
_kinds: A queue holds more than bugs. The fleet dashboard's request_capability
tool files a kind and encodes the choice as a TAG; LeapHQ built a
separate table for the same idea, so a fleet feature request arrived in
core's BUGS list mislabelled. `kind` is a first-class field so both can
say the same thing, derived from tags because every row predates it.
TWO kinds, not three. `capability` was retired in the fleet dashboard on
2026-09-16 (its PR #225, 'a new ability of the agent's is a feature
request like any other') and its tool's enum is now bug|feature. This
contract briefly declared three, drafted from a survey taken before that
landed — the mirror into that repo is what caught it, which is the
argument for mirroring early rather than at the end. A contract derived
from implementations defers to them when they decide something.
`capability-request` therefore survives as a LEGACY TAG that maps to
`feature`: those rows keep the tag they were written with, and read as
_app: WHICH QUEUE a report came from, on a merged list: `leaphq`, `fleet`,
`report`. Stamped by the federating reader, never by the filer.
This was called `source` until v2, which collided head-on with the
`source-on-every-report` pattern, where `source` is the FILER'S SURFACE
triage can route by device class. Two meanings, one name, and a
conformance table claiming the pattern was satisfied because the name was
present. Renaming was a one-consumer edit while this contract lived in one
repo; after mirroring it would be a five-repo edit. Hence now.
`source` is therefore RESERVED and deliberately unimplemented — the name
is freed, the feature is not built. Do not reuse it for anything else.
_summaryFields: Every field a LIST row must carry. The federation adapter used to drop
details and metaBuildSha on the way in, so a plug-in report reached core
without the one piece of metadata the pattern calls most useful. Anything
`screenshot` is a BOOLEAN — 'is there one' — never a path or a URL. The
bytes live in the filing app's own store and are fetched separately, so
a list row must not carry them. This field was drafted as
`hasScreenshot` from LeapHQ's internal shape and renamed within the day:
mirroring the fixture into the fleet dashboard showed that all four
bug-report-py apps emit `screenshot`, and a contract should speak the
name its implementations already use. Found BY doing the mirror, which
is the argument for doing it before the fixture spreads.
_detailFields: What a DETAIL read adds on top of the summary. Every store already keeps
all of it; until 2026-09-16 LeapHQ's triage screen rendered none of it and
had no detail route at all, so a bug report could only be read as its own
`transcript` is OPTIONAL and the only field here a store may legitimately
not have: bug-report-py keeps one (the fleet's agent attaches the last 5
chat turns when it files on itself), LeapHQ does not collect one yet. A
reader must RENDER it where it exists — it was stored by four apps and
displayed by none, which is worse than not collecting it. Everything else
_outOfScope: The canonical pattern's v2 sketch also proposes a free-form
`context: object` and an `attachments[]` array. Deliberately NOT here:
no app in this suite has either, and adding speculative fields to a
contract five repos must honour is the same mistake as extracting a
shared implementation early. Add them when a second app wants one.
_auditFields: One row per transition. The actor is the authenticated caller, never the body.
_limits: Server-enforced, not client. Shared by every store.
_example: A complete record in the wire shape. Both sides round-trip THIS object:
the serialiser must be able to emit it, the renderer must be able to
display it without inventing or dropping a field.

example.title: Hour picker sticks on the second tap
example.details: Tapping 7.5 twice leaves the picker open and the value unset.
example.metaUserAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_5 like Mac OS X)
